reasoning_traces.think:
The core idea of the paper is to assign credit for shot-ending actions in football using a restricted Shapley value approach. It defines a model-based worth function υ(S) that evaluates the expected goals (xGA) contributed by a coalition S of players. For observed coalitions, this is computed as the sum of predicted xGA over all relevant shots involving those players. For unobserved coalitions, it uses a single out-of-sample prediction from an XGBoost model. The restricted Shapley value φ_i^R(υ) then computes each player's marginal contribution by averaging over compatible subsets of coalitions, weighted by combinatorial probabilities adjusted for the restricted support. This yields a fair allocation of credit even when not all possible coalitions are observed. The studentized version PRSV_i = φ̂_i^R / SE(φ̂_i^R) provides a normalized signal-to-noise ratio for comparing players. The method assumes passing networks define coalitions, excludes off-ball activity, and does not account for causal effects beyond descriptive attribution. Its dual nature—combining game-theoretic fairness with statistical robustness—makes it suitable for both GSI’s Bayesian inference pipelines and GSE’s situational reasoning engines.
